newsitem.title: USA: Dollar continues advance against yen and mark.
newsitem.headline: Dollar continues advance against yen and mark.

text.p: The dollar rose Wednesday, briefly trading above 112 yen for the first time since January 1994, as Japanese investors continued to reject the skimpy yields of yen-denominated investments.

The yen's slide was later offset by a falling mark, which hit its lowest level against the dollar in more than three months after New York Federal Reserve Chairman John Whitehead predicted further dollar appreciation against the mark but not the yen.

"He said dollar/yen was (near a top) and that the mark and European currencies could depreciate between 5 and 10 percent against the dollar," said Bill Bertha, chief dealer at Mellon Bank. "So they cracked the mark against yen pretty hard."

The dollar rose to 112.10 yen in New York, getting an extra lift after Japanese Finance Minister Waturu Kubo retracted a statement he made in New York earlier this week. But it settled at 111.87 yen, up from 111.43 yen at Tuesday's close.
Against the mark, the dollar rose to 1.5325 marks, its best performance since June 25, when it reached 1.5350. The dollar closed at 1.5263 marks Tuesday.

Before returning to Japan after attending a gathering of G7 finance and central bank officials in Washington, Kubo was quoted Monday as saying he favoured a "strong" but not necessarily a "stronger" dollar. But he said Wednesday his remark had been misinterpreted.
But comments from G7 officials early this week favouring a strong dollar have been overshadowed by substantial capital outflows from Japan and yen-denominated investments.

Japanese money managers are battling to offer Japan's huge pension funds better investment returns than can be found in domestic markets, where short-term interest rates are a mere 0.5 percent, observers said.

"The market just senses the dollar is bid (being bought) and will remain so until we see some of these investment flows slow or until the Bank of Japan hints it is close to an interest rate hike," said David Gilmore, a partner at Foreign Exchange Analytics.
In other trading, the dollar rose to 1.2579 Swiss francs from 1.2555 Swiss on Tuesday and fell to Canadian $1.3593 from C$1.3597.
The pound was at $1.5653, down from $1.5650.
